offending.quoted_text: OCGA § 9-15-14 … authorizes the recovery of attorney's fees … [in] an appeal
offending.filing: Appellee's Brief, Court of Appeals of Georgia (request for appellate attorney's fees)
offending.court_quote: We cannot find the cited case, Johnson v. Johnson, either by case name or citation. And, not surprisingly, we could not locate the case by its purported holding, which is a blatant misstatement of the law. More than 30 years ago, this Court held that “OCGA § 9-15-14 does not authorize the imposition of attorney fees and expenses of litigation for proceedings before an appellate court of this state.”
offending.quote_locator: slip op. at 6 and Appendix (slip op. at 13)
offending.what_actually_exists: Nothing. The purported holding also misstates settled Georgia law, which holds OCGA § 9-15-14 does not authorise appellate attorney fees.

offending.quoted_text: The trial court's findings of fact will not be set aside unless they are clearly erroneous, and the appellate court must defer to the trial court's ability to assess witness credibility.

offending.court_quote: According to Appellee's Brief, Wilson supports deference to the trial court, specifically “The trial court's findings of fact will not be set aside unless they are clearly erroneous, and the appellate court must defer to the trial court's ability to assess witness credibility.” However, Wilson says nothing about appellate review of a trial court's factual findings. See 282 Ga. 728 (653 SE2d 702) (2007).
offending.what_actually_exists: Wilson v. Wilson, 282 Ga. 728 (653 SE2d 702) (2007) is real but says nothing about appellate review of a trial court's factual findings.
